decisions.reason: The fouling detection automation is still early in its life, builds on existing automation modules, and costs little to keep, while its value in energy-recovery applications remains uncertain.
The weir dimensioning web tool is cheap to maintain and generates leads with engineering planners for the core weir business, especially now that the new weir products D and F are on the market.
The fouling detection system overlaps with Product A and may later be merged with it, but the evidence is still too thin to justify abandoning an option that costs little to keep.
The spring-controlled flap weir was launched only in 2024, sits close to the firm's established hydraulic steel offer, and its market response is not yet known, so the option stays open.
The energy management system fits the firm's strategic direction toward digital networking and energy efficiency, and its value is still uncertain but potentially high, so keeping it is worthwhile.
The overflow flap gate line has its own website page and several models, which signals a deliberate commitment close to the core business, so dropping it after one year would be premature.
